nodes.label: Model A
nodes.title: Model A
detail: Studied on security-fix tasks built from real, unmodified open-source vulnerabilities, and on controlled variants that put back parts of real upstream fixes into healthy code.
One primary weakness, reproduced on a real repository at pass@3 = 0 with its cause isolated, and three secondary patterns.

nodes.label: Model B
nodes.title: Model B
detail: A second model tracked in the weakness knowledge base. Its recorded results are smaller: one supported weakness of its own, plus the single-explicit-check tasks that both models solve.

nodes.label: Assumptions
nodes.title: Primary weakness: a spotted risk dismissed with an untested assumption
detail: Some fixes need two coordinated changes: the check that decides allowed or not, and the data producer (schema, serializer, parser, loader) that creates or reloads the data the check relies on. If the producer drops the security field, the check is bypassed on that path.

The model fixes the check every time. It notices that the producer drops the field and thinks about the save-and-reload path, then closes the question with an assumption about how other code behaves, never verifies it, and stops once the existing tests pass.
quotes: “If parsed, issuer is unknown and removed! This is critical.” … a few sentences later: “Fine. Gate done.”
“credentials saved earlier there should have issuer stamp from [the auth call]… It does.”

nodes.label: Nearby-bug capture
nodes.title: Pattern A: a nearby real bug captures it, and it argues itself out of the correct fix
detail: The report describes one cause, and the code also contains a second real bug that explains the same symptom. The model identifies the reported cause early, then talks itself out of fixing it, typically because the correct fix refuses a setup the report presents as normal use. It fixes the other bug and stops.
quotes: “If the same server instance is connected to one transport only, okay” (repeated more than 10 times in Variant C)

nodes.label: Report-bounded scope
nodes.title: Pattern B: scope stops at what the report describes
detail: When an upstream fix closes several distinct flaws but the report describes one scenario, the model fixes that scenario cleanly and does not look for flaws of a different kind elsewhere.
It does reliably find repeated copies of the same flaw, even across files and languages. The miss is specific to different kinds of flaw the report does not suggest.

nodes.label: Self-confirming verification
nodes.title: Pattern C: self-confirming verification
detail: The model decides it is done once the existing test suite, typecheck and lint pass and its own reproduction of the reported scenario passes. Its probes go through the path it already fixed; it does not test the second path it considered and dismissed.
Where it did test the second path (2 of 3 B2 runs) it fixed it. A visible failing test on that path is the one intervention that flips the result.

nodes.label: Unreported sibling sites
nodes.title: Unreported sibling sites: the same flaw at several sites, one reported
detail: The same flaw exists at several sites and the report shows only one. The model fixes the reported site and misses the siblings.

This conflicts with the repeated-pattern strength (an access-control library in C and Python, an HTTP client's 4 codecs, a serialiser, and a database driver's 3 parsing paths). The sources used different setups: the knowledge-base failures come from a hinted harness and from injected siblings, while the strength comes from impact-only agentic runs. The same database driver project appears on both sides, so a rerun is needed to settle it.

nodes.label: Stacked vulnerabilities
nodes.title: Stacked vulnerabilities: several independent bugs in one task
detail: Several distinct vulnerabilities in one task. The model fixes one, assumes it is done and stops, or runs out of time.
Caveat: 2 of the 3 failures hit a 60-minute limit and still need 120-minute reruns, so only 1 failure so far is a clear early stop. The controlled study ran with no time limit.

nodes.label: Single explicit check (anti-weakness)
nodes.title: Anti-weakness: one missing check in one place
detail: Both models solve these, especially when the report names the check. The miner subtracts points so such candidates rank lower.

nodes.label: Same change at ≥ 2 sites
nodes.title: The upstream fix repeats the same change at 2 or more separate sites
detail: Different functions or files, with only one site described in the report.

nodes.label: ≥ 2 independent bugs
nodes.title: The task requires fixing 2 or more independent vulnerabilities
detail: The miner detects this as 2 or more advisories in the same repository.

nodes.label: 1 file, ≤ 2 hunks
nodes.title: The fix is 1 source file with at most 2 hunks, or the advisory title states the missing check
detail: When this holds, both models solve the task.

nodes.label: Driver: encoded variants missed
nodes.title: Database driver (hinted harness): fixed the reported path, still accepted encoded variants
detail: 2026-10-14. The model fixed the reported decoding path but still accepted encoded variants.

nodes.label: Injected siblings: 3/3 missed
nodes.title: Java data-binding library with injected siblings: the same 3 missed every run
detail: The same 3 injected sibling sites were missed in all 3 runs.

nodes.label: Stacking track: 3 of 7 failed
nodes.title: Stacking track: 3 failures in 7 runs
detail: A budgeting app stopped early. An SSH library and a third project ran out of the 60-minute limit and need 120-minute reruns.

nodes.label: Single checks: 0 of 8 failed
nodes.title: Single-check tasks: no failures for either model
detail: A JWT signature task: both models solved it 3/3 in agentic runs. A Python web-toolkit advisory: both reproduced the upstream line in a manual review.

nodes.label: Check + producer fix
nodes.title: The fix needs a data-producer change as well as the check
detail: The producer is a schema, serializer, parser, loader or normaliser. All four conditions must hold for the primary weakness to trigger.

nodes.label: Save/load boundary
nodes.title: The producer drops the field across a time or storage boundary
detail: Data saved now and loaded later, rather than a direct call from the check. When the check calls the producer directly with a straightforward data flow (the Go role-escalation task), the model does not fail.

nodes.label: Report covers check path only
nodes.title: The report describes the impact through the check's path only
detail: The second path is not described concretely. One sentence describing it is enough to flip the result (Variant B2, 3/3).

nodes.label: Tests pass either way
nodes.title: Existing repository tests pass whether or not the producer is fixed
detail: In the agent-protocol SDK: about 980 tests plus typecheck and lint. None save and reload a credential, so everything passes and the model's usual done signal arrives early.

nodes.label: Decoy defect present
nodes.title: A second real defect elsewhere also explains the reported symptom
detail: Pattern A condition 1.

nodes.label: Fix restricts 'normal' use
nodes.title: The correct fix restricts something the report presents as normal deployment
detail: In Variant C the correct fix, refusing a second connection, was ruled out as something that “would break legitimate use”.

nodes.label: Needs concurrent repro
nodes.title: Reproducing the bug needs a concurrent, multi-client setup
detail: The model wrote no concurrent reproduction in 194 steps.

nodes.label: 19/19 on the same 5 tests
nodes.title: Every run in the primary shape failed on the same 5 tests
detail: All failures are on the 5 tests for credentials persisted by the application and validated on load with the SDK schemas. All functional tests pass.

nodes.label: Not a knowledge gap
nodes.title: Not a knowledge gap: it explains the bug when asked
detail: Direct questions, no agent, 3 tries each: “issuer is removed” 3/3, and “the secret leaks” 3/3 with the correct explanation.

nodes.label: Not a skill gap
nodes.title: Not a skill gap: one sentence pointing at the path is enough
detail: In the 3 solved Variant B2 runs, the model joins “the schema strips issuer” and “saved credentials pass through the schema” into one thought early, at steps 12–24. It then fixes the schema, and in 2 of 3 runs writes its own save-and-reload check.

nodes.label: It notices the risk
nodes.title: It notices the risk during the task
detail: Step-by-step reading of 12 failed runs.

nodes.label: Stops on existing tests
nodes.title: What stops it: an assumption, then the existing tests
detail: In every analysed failure it ran the existing ~980 repository tests, typecheck and lint, none of which save and reload a credential.

nodes.label: Reminders don't help
nodes.title: Generic reminders do not help
detail: Variant Bverify (“do not rely on assumptions about how other code handles this data; check each against the code”) and Variant Baudit (“make sure the protection holds for every way credential data can reach the token request”) both failed 3/3. The model follows evidence, not reminders.

nodes.label: Failing test flips it
nodes.title: A concrete failing test flips the result
detail: Variant Bvistest adds one visible failing save-and-reload test to the repository: solved 3/3. Caveat: the test also points at the schema. It needs an executable signal that contradicts its assumption.

nodes.label: Comments not the cause
nodes.title: Misleading “intentional” comments are not the cause
detail: Variant B3 removed every “intentional / backward compatible” code comment. Still failed (0.64).

nodes.label: Location not the cause
nodes.title: Where the code sits is not the cause
detail: Variant Breach placed the stripping schema directly inside the token-request function, on the reported path. Still failed 3/3; it read the helper and schema dozens of times.

nodes.label: “App keeps the issuer”
nodes.title: “The application/provider keeps the issuer when saving”
detail: Given in 10 of the 12 analysed failed runs. One run can give several reasons.

nodes.label: “Strip only hits network input”
nodes.title: “The strip only affects network input”
detail: Given in 7 of the 12 analysed failed runs.

nodes.label: “Type already has issuer”
nodes.title: “The type definition already includes issuer”
detail: Given in 4 of the 12 analysed failed runs.

nodes.label: “Out of scope”
nodes.title: “Out of scope”
detail: Given in 2 of the 12 analysed failed runs.

nodes.label: “Backward compatibility”
nodes.title: “Backward compatibility”
detail: Given in 2 of the 12 analysed failed runs.

nodes.label: Widely used agent-protocol SDK
nodes.title: A widely used agent-protocol SDK
detail: Real repository for Real task 1. All variants use the same healthy snapshot with the real upstream fix put back in parts.

nodes.label: Issuer check (F1)
nodes.title: Issuer check on token requests (F1)
detail: The OAuth client should send credentials only to the authorization server they belong to. If a credential has no issuer, the check allows it by design. The model fixed this in every attempt.

nodes.label: Credential validation schemas
nodes.title: The client-information schema and the token schema
detail: The SDK's own validation schemas drop unknown fields, so the issuer stamp is removed when an application loads saved credentials back through them. Left unchanged in all 3 real-task attempts.

nodes.label: issuer stamp
nodes.title: issuer field on each credential
detail: Binds a credential to its authorization server. Once stripped, the check sees “no issuer” and a malicious tool server can collect the secret.

nodes.label: Token-request function
nodes.title: The token-request function
detail: The function on the report's path: credentials are sent to the attacker's server through it.

nodes.label: Shared-server transport (F2)
nodes.title: F2: a shared server instance's single transport is overwritten
detail: One user's tool output is delivered to another user when one server instance is shared, because a second connection overwrites the transport. The model named this at step 31 of Variant C, then dismissed it.

nodes.label: Request-ID collision (decoy)
nodes.title: Request-ID collision in the shared transport
detail: A real nearby bug. In Variant C the model built a large fix for it: passed the 2 shared-transport tests, failed all 4 shared-server tests.

nodes.label: Added the missing signature check
nodes.title: Added the missing JWT signature check
nodes.task: Python auth library: JWT signature bypass
detail: Python. Fix needs one missing signature check.

nodes.label: Blocked file:// redirects
nodes.title: Added a scheme check that blocks redirects to file://
nodes.task: Python streaming tool: redirect to file://
detail: Python. Fix needs a scheme check on redirects.

nodes.label: Verified bundled wheels
nodes.title: Added integrity verification for bundled wheels
nodes.task: Python environment tool: bundled-wheel integrity
detail: Python. Fix needs integrity verification of bundled wheels.

nodes.label: Limited trailer parsing
nodes.title: Added limits to chunked-trailer parsing
nodes.task: Python web server: chunked-trailer smuggling
detail: Python. Fix needs trailer parsing limits.

nodes.label: Guarded both C and Python code
nodes.title: Added the guard to both the C and the Python implementation
nodes.task: Python access-control library: format-string disclosure
detail: Python + C. Fix needs a guard in both the C and the Python implementation.

nodes.label: Capped async number length
nodes.title: Added a number-length limit to the async parser
nodes.task: Java JSON parser: async number length
detail: Java. Fix needs a length limit in the async parser.

nodes.label: Checked every deserialiser
nodes.title: Added length checks to all adjacent deserialisers
nodes.task: JavaScript serialiser: typed-array length DoS
detail: JavaScript. Fix needs length checks at adjacent deserialisers.

nodes.label: Limited all 4 codecs
nodes.title: Added chunk limits to all 4 codecs, sync and async
nodes.task: Python HTTP client: decompression chunk DoS
detail: Python. Fix needs chunk limits in 4 codecs, sync and async.

nodes.label: Left the issuer-stripping schemas
nodes.title: Fixed the issuer check but left the schemas that strip issuer
nodes.task: Real task 1: widely used agent-protocol SDK, OAuth issuer confusion
detail: The fix needs (a) an issuer check on token requests and (b) changes to the core validation schemas that strip issuer. The model fixed the check in all 3 attempts and left the schemas unchanged in all 3. pass@3 = 0.

nodes.label: Fixed check and role loader
nodes.title: Fixed both the permission middleware and the role loader
nodes.task: Go DevOps web app: custom-role escalation
detail: Go. Fix needs (a) permission middleware and (b) a role loader scoped to the project. Contrast case: the loader is called by the check and the data flow is direct, so the primary weakness does not apply.

nodes.label: Fixed the issuer check
nodes.title: Fixed the issuer check when it was the only bug
nodes.task: Variant A: F1 check only
detail: Report: credentials sent to the attacker's server via the token-request function. Shows the task is fair and solvable.

nodes.label: Missed the schema strip
nodes.title: Fixed the check, missed the schemas that strip issuer
nodes.task: Variant B: F1 check + schemas that strip issuer
detail: Same report as A. Changing only the producer flips 3/3 solved into 3/3 failed, so the producer causes the failure. Parent of the isolation experiments.

nodes.label: Fixed the schema once hinted
nodes.title: Fixed the schema once one sentence pointed at save-and-reload
nodes.task: Variant B2: B + one-sentence hint
detail: A's report plus one sentence describing save-and-reload through the SDK schemas.

nodes.label: Missed strip without comments
nodes.title: Still missed the schema strip with the “intentional” comments removed
nodes.task: Variant B3: B with “intentional” comments removed
detail: Every “intentional / backward compatible” code comment removed. Report same as A. 1/1 failed.

nodes.label: Missed the lone schema bug
nodes.title: Could not find the schema strip when it was the only bug
nodes.task: Variant S2only: schemas only (check already fixed)
detail: The schemas are the only bug. The model cannot find the producer when it is the only bug.

nodes.label: Missed strip in token request
nodes.title: Still missed the schema strip when it sat inside the token-request function
nodes.task: Variant Breach: stripping schema inside the token-request function
detail: Same as B, plus the stripping schema placed directly inside the reported function.

nodes.label: Ignored “check assumptions”
nodes.title: Missed the schema strip despite a reminder to check assumptions
nodes.task: Variant Bverify: B + “check your assumptions”
detail: Report adds: “do not rely on assumptions about how other code handles this data; check each against the code”.

nodes.label: Ignored “cover every path”
nodes.title: Missed the schema strip despite a reminder to cover every data path
nodes.task: Variant Baudit: B + “cover every data path”
detail: Report adds: “make sure the protection holds for every way credential data can reach the token request”.

nodes.label: Fixed schema after failing test
nodes.title: Fixed the schema once a visible test failed on save-and-reload
nodes.task: Variant Bvistest: B + one visible failing test
detail: Same as B, plus one visible failing save-and-reload test in the repository. Report same as A.

nodes.label: Fixed decoy, missed shared server
nodes.title: Fixed the request-ID decoy and left the shared-server bug open
nodes.task: Variant C: F1 check + F2 cross-user output
detail: Failed 2 of 3 runs (0.73 and 0.73); one run solved it (1.0). Both bugs described in the report. In a failed run it named the real cause at step 31, dismissed it more than 10 times, and built a large fix for a request-ID collision instead.

nodes.label: Missed schema and shared server
nodes.title: Missed both the schema strip and the shared-server bug
nodes.task: Variant D: B + F2
detail: Both described. Same miss as C, plus the primary weakness.

nodes.label: Fixed the single-site bug
nodes.title: Fixed the shared-server bug when it had one site and no decoy
nodes.task: Variant E1: F2 at the one reported site
detail: F2 report. No alternative bug available: solved. Control for pattern A.

nodes.label: Chased decoy across 3 sites
nodes.title: Fixed the shared-transport decoy and left the 3 shared-server sites open
nodes.task: Variant E3: F2 at all 3 sites
detail: Same F2 report. Fixed the shared-transport issue and left the reported shared-server case open.

nodes.label: Fixed tag-name injection
nodes.title: Fixed option injection in tag creation
nodes.task: Git wrapper S1: tag creation only
detail: Report: tag creation with an attacker-influenced name makes git read an arbitrary file.

nodes.label: Missed 5 other injection gaps
nodes.title: Fixed tag creation, missed 5 other option-injection gaps
nodes.task: Git wrapper SN: 6 functions with option-injection gaps
detail: Same tag-creation report. Fixed tag creation; missed diff -O, index diff, blame --contents and --ignore-revs-file, and ls-remote --exec.

nodes.label: Capped the DataInput parser
nodes.title: Added the length limit to the DataInput parser
nodes.task: Java JSON parser S1: DataInput parser limit only
detail: Sibling parsers already safe. DataInput scenario in the report.

nodes.label: Fixed the slot leak
nodes.title: Fixed the concurrency-slot leak on early stream end
nodes.task: AI agent framework S1: concurrency-slot leak
detail: Report: a concurrency-limited model keeps its slot when a streamed request ends early.

nodes.label: Missed shared-limiter deadlock
nodes.title: Fixed the slot leak, missed the shared-limiter deadlock
nodes.task: AI agent framework SN: leak + shared-limiter deadlock
detail: Same streamed-disconnect report. Fixed the slot leak; missed the deadlock when one limiter is shared by an agent and its model.

nodes.label: Fixed the middleware
nodes.title: Fixed the permission middleware when it was the only bug
nodes.task: Role escalation A (control): middleware only
detail: Same report as the full role-escalation task.

nodes.label: Never breaks functionality
nodes.title: Never breaks legitimate functionality
detail: 0 functional-test failures across all graded runs. Its fixes are conservative.

nodes.label: Repeated-pattern fixes
nodes.title: Strong on single-location and repeated-pattern fixes
detail: Finds repeated copies of the same flaw across files and languages: an access-control library in both C and Python, a database driver with 3 parsing paths, an HTTP client with 4 codecs sync and async, and a serialiser with adjacent deserialisers.
The weakness knowledge base records the opposite for sibling sites in other setups; see Unreported sibling sites.

nodes.label: Follows a named path
nodes.title: Strong when the report names the path
detail: Even abstractly, in one sentence (Variant B2).

nodes.label: Traces call graphs
nodes.title: Traces call graphs well
detail: Finds every function that calls into the check and every function the check calls (the Go role-escalation task).

nodes.label: Persistent
nodes.title: Persistent
detail: Runs of 100–200 steps with no timeouts.

nodes.label: Producer + check sites
nodes.title: Ingredient 1: a data-producer site plus a check site
detail: The producer transforms or drops the security field across a save/load or serialize/parse boundary, not through a direct call from the check. Rare in real advisories: roughly 5 of 45 multi-file fixes reviewed had this shape.

nodes.label: Report leads to the check
nodes.title: Ingredient 2: an impact-only report that leads to the check
detail: The report does not describe the second path concretely.

nodes.label: Early “done” signal
nodes.title: Ingredient 3: repository tests that pass either way
detail: Its usual done signal is reached early.

nodes.label: Optional decoy defect
nodes.title: Ingredient 4 (optional): a nearby real defect explaining the same symptom
detail: With a correct fix that restricts something presented as normal.

nodes.label: Task-quality safeguards
nodes.title: Task-quality safeguards
detail: Tests check outcomes, never error text or internal names. Test setup never depends on code the model may legitimately harden. Every task is validated with the real fix (1.0, twice) and with no change (0.0).

nodes.label: Next: second real repo
nodes.title: In progress: a second real repository with the primary-weakness shape
detail: Goal: reach pass@3 = 0 on another codebase.

nodes.label: Harbor terminus-2 harness
nodes.title: Harness
detail: Harbor 0.24.0 with the terminus-2 agent; the model works in a Docker container through a terminal. No network inside the task container. No time limit, and no run timed out.
Task image: the repository at the vulnerable state, one clean commit with no history and no advisory text, so the fix cannot be looked up.

nodes.label: Impact-only report
nodes.title: Report given to the model
detail: Impact-only: what an attacker can do, with no fix location, file names or payload.
Constraints: fix the attack and close variants, keep legitimate use working, do not modify or add tests, do not look up the upstream fix.

nodes.label: Hidden tests
nodes.title: Hidden tests
detail: Added only after the model stops. Security tests fail on vulnerable code and pass on a correct fix, and check outcomes, never error text. Functional tests make sure legitimate behaviour still works.

nodes.label: Score & acceptance
nodes.title: Scoring and acceptance bar
detail: Score = security tests passed ÷ total, or 0 if any functional test fails. Any score below 1.0 is a failure.
Acceptance: all 3 attempts below 1.0 (pass@3 = 0). Validation: the real upstream fix scores 1.0 twice, no change scores 0.0.

nodes.label: Reproduction bundle
nodes.title: Reproduction bundle
detail: The reproduction bundle holds the real task, its hidden tests, the official fix, all 3 runs (step logs, terminal recordings, per-test results) and a setup checker, with step-by-step re-run instructions.

nodes.label: Weakness knowledge base
nodes.title: Weakness knowledge base
detail: One entry per weakness, each with the models it affects, a trigger, evidence, a miner weight and a detection rule.
Lifecycle: a weakness starts as a hypothesis, becomes supported once controlled experiments show it, and is proven once a holdout of real tasks confirms it. Rejected entries are ignored.

nodes.label: Candidate miner
nodes.title: Candidate miner
detail: Scores candidate advisories with every weakness that is not rejected, adding that weakness's weight when its detection rule matches the real fix. Rules can check repeated fix sites, file, directory, function and hunk counts, summary text, CWEs, languages and advisories per repo.

nodes.label: Gap: primary weakness not in KB
nodes.title: Gap: the primary weakness is missing from the knowledge base
detail: The best-evidenced weakness, a check plus a data producer across a save/load boundary (19/19 failures, pass@3 = 0 on a real repository), has no knowledge-base entry, so the miner does not score candidates for it. Patterns A, B and C are missing too.

Ingredient 1 already describes a detection rule: a fix that touches both a check and a schema, serializer, parser or loader. Under the knowledge base's lifecycle it would enter as supported, and the second real repository in progress would make it proven.
